Medical Decision

Source: R/decision.h.R
decision.Rd

Function for Medical Decision Analysis. Sensitivity, Specificity, Positive Predictive Value, Negative Predictive Value.

Usage

decision(
  data,
  referenceType = "legacy",
  referenceDescription = "",
  targetDefinition = "",
  gold = NULL,
  goldPositive,
  newtest = NULL,
  testPositive,
  goldNegative,
  testNegative,
  pp = FALSE,
  pprob = 0.3,
  od = FALSE,
  fnote = FALSE,
  ci = FALSE,
  fagan = FALSE,
  faganColors = "jamovi",
  showNaturalLanguage = FALSE,
  showClinicalInterpretation = FALSE,
  showReportTemplate = FALSE,
  showAboutAnalysis = FALSE,
  showMisclassified = FALSE,
  maxCasesShow = 50,
  showValidationContext = FALSE,
  cohortRole = "",
  samplingDesign = "",
  thresholdSource = "",
  modelVersion = "",
  analysisUnit = "slide"
)

Arguments

data

The data as a data frame. The data frame should contain the variables specified in the 'variables' option.

referenceType

Comparator interpretation; legacy preserves existing binary calculations. Consensus and method report agreement without disease-risk interpretation.

referenceDescription

.

targetDefinition

.

gold

The reference standard variable, used as each case's disease status.

goldPositive

The positive reference level; disease interpretation requires a disease standard. It is never taken from the order of the levels: NULL leaves the analysis pending, listing the levels found. The argument has no default; pass the level.

newtest

The diagnostic test variable being evaluated for performance.

testPositive

The level representing a positive result for the test under evaluation. It is never taken from the order of the levels: NULL leaves the analysis pending, listing the levels found. The argument has no default; pass the level.

goldNegative

The level indicating absence of disease in the gold standard variable. The compiler forbids a default on a Level option, so R callers must pass it explicitly; pass NULL only for a two-level variable, where it is inferred. With three or more levels a NULL raises an error rather than pooling them.

testNegative

The level representing a negative result for the test under evaluation. The compiler forbids a default on a Level option, so R callers must pass it explicitly; pass NULL only for a two-level variable, where it is inferred. With three or more levels a NULL raises an error rather than pooling them.

pp

Boolean selection whether to use known population prevalence instead of study prevalence.

pprob

Population disease prevalence as a proportion strictly between 0 and 1.

od

Boolean selection whether to show original data frequency tables. The raw data outputs (rawContingency, rawCounts and missingDataSummary) are filled only when this is TRUE, so R code that reads them must set od = TRUE.

fnote

Boolean selection whether to show detailed explanatory footnotes.

ci

Boolean selection whether to calculate and display 95 percent confidence intervals.

fagan

Boolean selection whether to generate a Fagan nomogram plot.

faganColors

Colors of the Fagan nomogram's lines: "jamovi" follows the global palette, "classic" draws the positive-result line red and the negative-result line blue.

showNaturalLanguage

Boolean selection whether to show the natural language clinical summary.

showClinicalInterpretation

Boolean selection whether to show the clinical interpretation guide.

showReportTemplate

Boolean selection whether to show the copy-ready results paragraph.

showAboutAnalysis

Boolean selection whether to show the about analysis section.

showMisclassified

Boolean selection whether to show detailed misclassified cases tables.

maxCasesShow

Maximum number of misclassified cases to display in tables.

showValidationContext

.

cohortRole

.

samplingDesign

.

thresholdSource

.

modelVersion

.

analysisUnit

.

Value

A results object containing:

results$welcomea html
results$noticesa html
results$rawContingencya table
results$rawCountsa table
results$cTablea table
results$nTablea table
results$ratioTablea table
results$missingDataSummarya html
results$epirTable_ratioa table
results$epirTable_numbera table
results$plot1an image
results$naturalLanguageSummarya html
results$clinicalInterpretationa html
results$reportTemplatea html
results$aboutAnalysisa html
results$misclassifiedHeadinga html
results$confusionMatrixSummarya table
results$falsePositiveTablea table
results$falseNegativeTablea table
results$misclassificationInterpretationa html
results$saveClassificationsan output
results$referenceDefinitiona table
results$comparatorCountsa table
results$comparatorPopulationa table
results$comparatorMetricsa table
results$comparatorReporta html
results$comparatorCasesa table
results$validationContexta table

Tables can be converted to data frames with asDF or as.data.frame. For example:

results$rawContingency$asDF

as.data.frame(results$rawContingency)
